source.title: Irish News, 2 June 1961, p. 1 ("Castlereagh Rural Council"); Belfast News-Letter, 2 June 1961, p. 9 ("Results: county and rural council elections"); Belfast News-Letter, 17 May 1961, p. 5 ("Castlereagh: six of the nine seats may be contested (nominations)"); Belfast Telegraph, 7 June 1961, p. 16 ("Rural District of Castlereagh: election of councillors, 1961 (returning officer's notice of result, dated 5 June 1961)")
source.publisher: Irish News (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: All names and figures read on the Irish News, 2 June 1961, p. 1 (results by division with majority, spoiled votes, total poll and electorate); fuller forenames from the nominations, BNL 17 May 1961 p. 5 (gap-fill 6 Nov 2026).

note: Triennial election of Castlereagh Rural District Council, polled Thursday 1 June 1961. Six of the nine seats were contested. Of the six sitting official Unionists who faced contests only three held their seats: Castlereagh went to Labour, Ballyhackamore to the Tenants' Association and Ballycultra to an unofficial Unionist. The three uncontested divisions (Ballymiscaw, Craigavad, Dundonald) are from the returning officer's notice of result (Belfast Telegraph, 7 June 1961, p. 16), which also confirms the six contests (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). Printed: 'No change.' The News-Letter results print "James Gardner"; the Irish News results and both nomination lists print Gardiner.
